chunks: From him, from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Sa'id al-A'raj, who said:
I asked Aba 'Abdillah عليه السلام about a jar that holds one hundred ratls of water, into which one uqiyyah of blood falls: may I drink from it and perform wudu (ablution) with it? He said: "No."

key_terms.أُوقِيَّةٌ: a unit of weight, here referring to the amount of blood
key_terms.الْجَرَّةِ: a jar or large vessel used to hold water
key_terms.لَا: a clear negative ruling of prohibition or invalidity in this context
key_terms.مَاءٍ: water, the substance under legal discussion
key_terms.مِائَةَ رِطْلٍ: a measured quantity of one hundred ratls

ai.seo_question: Can water be used for drinking or wudu (ablution) if blood falls into it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning water contaminated by blood. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام rules that one may neither drink from such water nor use it for wudu (ablution), indicating its impurity and invalidity for ritual use.
